patron_of: Poitiers, children slow to learn, against snakebites
blurb: Bishop of Poitiers in Gaul (c. 310–367), exiled to Phrygia in 356 for refusing to condemn Athanasius. His De Trinitate made him the chief Latin opponent of Arianism; declared a Doctor in 1851.

patron_of: Nola, against perjury, eye diseases
blurb: Priest of Nola near Naples, imprisoned and tortured under Decius around 250, who survived and died in peace about 260. Paulinus of Nola wrote yearly poems at his tomb in the late 4th century.

key: St Paul the First Hermit, Confessor
patron_of: hermits, weavers, basket-makers
blurb: Egyptian who fled the Decian persecution around 250 to a cave in the Theban desert and stayed some ninety years, dying about 341. Jerome's Life records Antony's visit to him and the raven that brought bread.

patron_of: the sick, against gout and rheumatism, coppersmiths, charcoal-burners
blurb: Disciple of Benedict at Subiaco in the early 6th century; Gregory the Great tells how he ran across the lake to pull the boy Placid from the water. A 9th-century legend credits him with founding Glanfeuil in France.

patron_of: stable-hands, grooms
blurb: Pope from 308 to 309, who reorganized the Roman Church after the Diocletian persecution. His strict penances for apostates provoked riots, and Maxentius banished him; he died in exile that year.

patron_of: monks, hermits, domestic animals, swineherds, butchers, basket-makers, gravediggers, against skin diseases
blurb: Egyptian ascetic (251–356) who withdrew to the desert about 285 and drew the first communities of monks around him. Athanasius's Life of Antony, with its account of his temptations, spread monasticism across the Church.

key: Sts Marius, Martha, Audifax & Abachum, Martyrs
blurb: A Persian nobleman, his wife, and two sons who came to Rome about 270 to venerate the martyrs and bury the dead. Arrested under Claudius II; Martha was drowned and the men beheaded on the Via Cornelia.

patron_of: Denmark
blurb: Canute IV, king of Denmark from 1080, who enforced tithes and church law against resistance. Rebels killed him before the altar of St Alban's church at Odense on 10 July 1086; canonized 1101, Denmark's first saint.

patron_of: St Sebastian: athletes, soldiers, archers, plague; St Fabian: potters
prayer_title: Litany in Honour of Saint Sebastian
blurb: Fabian, pope from 236, was the first victim of the Decian persecution, executed 20 January 250. Sebastian, a soldier of Diocletian's guard, was shot with arrows about 288, survived, and was clubbed to death.

patron_of: young girls, chastity, virgins, betrothed couples, rape victims, gardeners
blurb: Roman girl of twelve or thirteen executed about 304 under Diocletian for refusing marriage and sacrifice, buried on the Via Nomentana. Ambrose, Damasus, and Prudentius wrote of her within a century; named in the Roman Canon.

patron_of: St Vincent: vintners, vinegar-makers, sailors, Lisbon, Valencia
blurb: Vincent, deacon of Saragossa, was tortured to death at Valencia in 304 under the governor Dacian. Anastasius, a Persian soldier turned monk, was strangled near the Euphrates in 628 under Chosroes II.

patron_of: canon lawyers, canonists, lawyers, medical record librarians
blurb: Catalan Dominican canonist (c. 1175–1275) who compiled the Decretals of Gregory IX in 1234, the standard code of church law for seven centuries. Third master general of the order; died at Barcelona aged nearly 100.

patron_of: against colic and stomach ache
blurb: Foster sister of Agnes, still a catechumen, stoned to death by a pagan crowd while praying at Agnes's tomb on the Via Nomentana about 304. Buried nearby; her name appears in the earliest Roman martyr lists.

patron_of: against stomach and intestinal ailments
blurb: Paul's companion from Lystra, recipient of two New Testament letters, and first bishop of Ephesus. Tradition records he was beaten to death about 97 after protesting a pagan festival in the city.

patron_of: against earache and dysentery
blurb: Bishop of Smyrna and disciple of the apostle John, burned alive in the city's stadium about 155 at the age of 86. The Martyrdom of Polycarp is the earliest surviving account of a Christian martyr's death.

key: St John Chrysostom, Bishop, Confessor & Doctor
patron_of: preachers, orators, lecturers, epileptics, Constantinople
blurb: Priest of Antioch and patriarch of Constantinople from 398 (c. 349–407), called 'golden-mouthed' for his preaching. His rebukes of court luxury led the Empress Eudoxia to exile him; he died on the road in Pontus.

patron_of: captives, prisoners, Mercedarians
blurb: Merchant from Languedoc (c. 1189–1256) who founded the Order of Our Lady of Mercy at Barcelona in 1218 to ransom Christians held captive by the Moors. Members vowed to offer themselves in exchange if needed.

patron_of: young girls, chastity, virgins, betrothed couples, rape victims, gardeners
blurb: The octave day of St Agnes, kept at Rome since at least the 7th century. The ancient Acts tell that eight days after her death she appeared to her parents at her tomb, surrounded by virgins and holding a lamb.

key: St Francis de Sales, Bishop, Confessor & Doctor
patron_of: writers, journalists, the Catholic press, the deaf, educators, confessors
prayer_title: Litany in Honour of St. Francis de Sales
blurb: Bishop of Geneva (1567–1622), resident at Annecy, who reconverted the Chablais from Calvinism and wrote the Introduction to the Devout Life. Co-founded the Visitation nuns with Jane de Chantal in 1610; Doctor 1877.

patron_of: Rome, nursing mothers
prayer_title: Novena to Saint Martina of Rome
blurb: Roman virgin martyred traditionally under Alexander Severus about 228. Her relics were found in 1634 beneath her church at the Forum, and Urban VIII rebuilt the church and composed hymns for her office.

patron_of: youth, apprentices, editors, publishers, schoolchildren, magicians, Salesians
blurb: Piedmontese priest (1815–1888) who gathered the working boys of Turin into oratories and trade schools. Founded the Salesians in 1859 and, with Mary Mazzarello, the Salesian Sisters; canonized 1934.

key: Purification of the Blessed Virgin Mary
blurb: Candlemas, 2 February: Mary's purification and the presentation of Jesus in the Temple forty days after his birth, when Simeon called him a light to the Gentiles. Kept at Jerusalem by the 380s; the candle procession is 7th-century Roman.

patron_of: throat ailments, wool-combers, veterinarians, wild animals, Dubrovnik
prayer_title: Novena in Honor of St. Blaise
blurb: Bishop of Sebaste in Armenia, torn with iron wool-combs and beheaded about 316 under Licinius. The legend that he saved a boy choking on a fishbone gave rise to the blessing of throats on his feast.

patron_of: against riots and sudden death, diplomats, Florence
blurb: Florentine Carmelite (1302–1374), bishop of Fiesole from 1349, known as a mediator between the warring factions of Tuscan cities. Urban V sent him to pacify Bologna; canonized 1629.

patron_of: breast cancer, nurses, bell-founders, bakers, against fire and earthquakes, Catania, Malta
blurb: Virgin of Catania in Sicily, tortured and killed about 251 under Decius after refusing the consul Quintianus; her breasts were cut off. Named in the Roman Canon; her veil is carried against eruptions of Etna.

patron_of: Crete
blurb: Greek convert and companion of Paul, who left him on Crete to organize the churches there and addressed an epistle to him. Tradition says he died in old age at Gortyna around the end of the 1st century.

patron_of: gardeners, florists, brewers, brides, newlyweds, midwives
blurb: Virgin of Caesarea in Cappadocia beheaded about 304 under Diocletian. The legend tells that a child brought roses and apples from paradise to the lawyer Theophilus, who had mocked her on the way to execution.

patron_of: Camaldolese
prayer_title: Prayer for the Feast of Saint Romuald, Abbot
blurb: Nobleman of Ravenna (c. 951–1027) who became a monk after his father killed a man in a duel. Founded the hermitage of Camaldoli about 1012, origin of the Camaldolese, joining hermit life to the Benedictine Rule.

key: St Cyril of Alexandria, Bishop, Confessor & Doctor
patron_of: Alexandria
blurb: Patriarch of Alexandria from 412 to 444, who presided at the Council of Ephesus in 431 and secured the condemnation of Nestorius. His defense of Mary as Theotokos defined the unity of Christ's person; Doctor 1882.

patron_of: dentists, toothache, dental diseases
blurb: Aged deaconess of Alexandria seized in an anti-Christian riot in 249; the mob broke out her teeth and she walked into the fire they had prepared. Her bishop Dionysius recorded the death in a letter preserved by Eusebius.

patron_of: nuns, Benedictine nuns, convulsive children, against storms and rain
prayer_title: Litany in Honour of St. Scholastica
blurb: Twin sister of Benedict (c. 480–543), who led a community of nuns near Monte Cassino. Gregory's Dialogues tell how her prayer brought a storm that kept Benedict talking with her the night before she died.

key: Apparition of the Immaculate Virgin Mary at Lourdes
prayer_title: Litany of Our Lady of Lourdes
blurb: Commemorates the eighteen apparitions to Bernadette Soubirous at the grotto of Massabielle between 11 February and 16 July 1858, where the Lady said 'I am the Immaculate Conception.' Pius X extended the feast to the whole Church in 1907.

key: Seven Holy Founders of the Servites, Confessors
prayer_title: Prayer for the Seven Holy Founders of the Servite Order
blurb: Seven Florentine merchants who left the city in 1233 for Monte Senario and founded the Servants of Mary, devoted to her sorrows. Alexis Falconieri, the last, died in 1310; all seven were canonized together in 1888.

patron_of: lovers, engaged couples, happy marriages, beekeepers, epilepsy, plague
blurb: Roman priest beheaded on the Via Flaminia about 269 under Claudius II and buried there, where a basilica stood by the 4th century. A bishop of Terni of the same name and day may be the same man.

key: St Peter Damian, Bishop, Confessor & Doctor
blurb: Hermit of Fonte Avellana (1007–1072), made cardinal bishop of Ostia in 1057 against his will. His Liber Gomorrhianus and legations attacked simony and clerical corruption before Gregory VII; Doctor 1828.

patron_of: alcoholics, carpenters, tailors, against smallpox
blurb: Chosen by lot to replace Judas among the Twelve before Pentecost (Acts 1), having followed Jesus from John's baptism. Later traditions place his preaching in Judea or Ethiopia; relics claimed at Trier since the 11th century.

key: St Gabriel of Our Lady of Sorrows, Confessor
patron_of: students, seminarians, clerics, young people, Abruzzi
blurb: Francesco Possenti of Assisi (1838–1862), who entered the Passionists at eighteen and died of tuberculosis at Isola del Gran Sasso before ordination, aged 24. Canonized 1920 as a model for young religious.

patron_of: Poland, Lithuania, youth, bachelors, princes
blurb: Prince of Poland (1458–1484), son of King Casimir IV, who declined the Hungarian crown offered him in 1471 and lived in chastity and prayer. Died of tuberculosis at Grodno aged 25; buried at Vilnius.

patron_of: Copenhagen
blurb: Pope from 253 to 254, banished under Gallus and soon recalled; continued Cornelius's mild policy toward Christians who had lapsed in persecution. Died peacefully but honored as a martyr; buried in the cemetery of Callixtus.

patron_of: mothers, expectant mothers, ranchers, butchers, Carthage
prayer_title: Novena to Saints Perpetua and Felicity
blurb: Perpetua, a 22-year-old noblewoman nursing an infant, and Felicitas, a slave who gave birth in prison, were killed by beasts in the amphitheater of Carthage on 7 March 203. Perpetua's own prison diary survives.

patron_of: students, universities, schools, theologians, philosophers, booksellers, pencil-makers, chastity
prayer_title: Litany in Honour of St. Thomas Aquinas
blurb: Dominican of Roccasecca (1225–1274), master at Paris and Naples, author of the Summa Theologiae and the Corpus Christi office. Died at Fossanova on his way to the Council of Lyon; Doctor 1567.

patron_of: motorists, Benedictine oblates, widows, Rome
blurb: Roman noblewoman (1384–1440), married forty years to Lorenzo Ponziani, who nursed the poor through plague and civil war. Founded the Oblates of Tor de' Specchi in 1425 and joined them after her husband died.
Forty soldiers of the Twelfth Legion left naked overnight on a frozen lake at Sebaste in Armenia in 320 under Licinius. One gave up; a guard took his place. Basil preached on them within fifty years.

key: St Gregory the Great, Pope, Confessor & Doctor
patron_of: musicians, singers, students, teachers, popes, masons, England, against plague
blurb: Roman prefect turned monk (c. 540–604), pope from 590, who sent Augustine to England in 596 and wrote the Pastoral Rule, Dialogues, and Moralia on Job. The Roman chant and liturgy bear his name.

patron_of: Ireland, engineers, against snakes, Nigeria, Boston, New York
blurb: Roman Briton (c. 385–461) enslaved in Ireland at sixteen, who escaped and returned about 432 as bishop to convert the island. His Confessio is the earliest Irish document; died at Saul near Downpatrick.

key: St Cyril of Jerusalem, Bishop, Confessor & Doctor
blurb: Bishop of Jerusalem from 350 (c. 315–386), exiled three times under Arian emperors. His Catechetical Lectures, given at the Holy Sepulchre, are the chief 4th-century witness to baptismal and eucharistic rites; Doctor 1882.

key: St Joseph, Spouse of the Blessed Virgin Mary
patron_of: the Universal Church, fathers, workers, carpenters, a happy death, the dying, families
blurb: Carpenter of Nazareth of David's line, husband of Mary and legal father of Jesus, who in Matthew's Gospel took the family to Egypt. His 19 March feast entered the Roman calendar under Sixtus IV in 1479.

patron_of: Europe, monks, students, farmers, against poison, witchcraft, temptations, the dying
prayer_title: Litany in Honour of St. Benedict
blurb: Born at Nursia (c. 480–547), hermit at Subiaco, founder of Monte Cassino about 529. His Rule became the norm of Western monasticism; 21 March marks his death, as told in Gregory's Dialogues.

patron_of: messengers, postal workers, telecommunications, diplomats, broadcasters, radio
prayer_title: Litany in Honour of St. Gabriel
blurb: The archangel who interpreted Daniel's visions and announced the births of John the Baptist and Jesus (Luke 1). Benedict XV added the feast to the universal calendar in 1921, placing it on the eve of the Annunciation.

key: Annunciation of the Blessed Virgin Mary
blurb: Gabriel's message to Mary at Nazareth and her consent, the moment of the Incarnation (Luke 1:26–38). Fixed on 25 March, nine months before Christmas; kept in the East by the 6th century and at Rome by the 7th.

patron_of: pharmacists, icon painters, theology students
blurb: Christian official of the caliph's court at Damascus (c. 675–749) who became a monk of Mar Saba near Jerusalem. His treatises defended holy images against iconoclasm; the Fount of Knowledge summed up Greek theology. Doctor 1890.

patron_of: military chaplains, jurists, judges, lawyers
prayer_title: Novena to Saint John of Capistrano
blurb: Franciscan preacher from the Abruzzi (1386–1456), lawyer and governor of Perugia before entering the order. At seventy he led a peasant army to the relief of Belgrade from the Turks in July 1456 and died at Ilok soon after.

patron_of: converts, Seville
prayer_title: Collect for the Feast of Saint Hermenegild
blurb: Visigothic prince, son of the Arian king Leovigild, converted to Catholicism by Bishop Leander of Seville about 579. After a failed revolt he was executed at Tarragona on 13 April 585 for refusing communion from an Arian bishop.

patron_of: philosophers, apologists, lecturers, orators
blurb: Philosopher from Flavia Neapolis in Samaria (c. 100–165) who taught Christianity at Rome in a philosopher's cloak. His two Apologies describe 2nd-century baptism and Eucharist; beheaded with six companions under Marcus Aurelius.

Valerian, husband of Cecilia, his brother Tiburtius, and Maximus, the officer converted at their execution, beheaded at Rome, traditionally about 230. Buried in the cemetery of Praetextatus on the Via Appia.

Syrian from Emesa, pope about 155 to 166, who received Polycarp at Rome and agreed to differ with him on the date of Easter. Opposed Valentinus and Marcion; honored as a martyr though no account of his death survives.

patron_of: theologians, Canterbury
blurb: Monk and abbot of Bec from Aosta (1033–1109), archbishop of Canterbury from 1093, twice exiled over lay investiture. His Proslogion framed the ontological argument and Cur Deus Homo the satisfaction theory of atonement; Doctor 1720.

Soter, pope about 166 to 175, praised by Dionysius of Corinth for Rome's alms to other churches. Caius, a Dalmatian, pope 283 to 296, buried in the cemetery of Callixtus. Both are honored as martyrs without record of violent death.

patron_of: England, soldiers, knights, archers, scouts, farmers, horsemen, against plague and skin disease
prayer_title: Litany in Honour of St. George
blurb: Soldier martyred at Lydda in Palestine about 303 under Diocletian; his cult there is attested by the 4th century. The dragon story is a medieval addition popularized by the Golden Legend after the Crusades.

patron_of: lawyers, missionaries
blurb: Swabian lawyer Mark Rey (1577–1622), who became a Capuchin and was sent to preach to the Calvinists of the Grisons. Killed by peasants at Seewis on 24 April 1622, the first martyr of Propaganda Fide; canonized 1746.

patron_of: Venice, notaries, lawyers, glaziers, prisoners, lions, Egypt
blurb: Author of the second Gospel, companion of Barnabas, Paul, and Peter, whose preaching he is said to have recorded. Tradition makes him founder of the church of Alexandria and martyr there about 68; Venice took his relics in 828.

patron_of: Germany, catechists, the Catholic press
blurb: Jesuit from Nijmegen (1521–1597), the first Dutchman in the Society, whose 1555 Catechism ran to hundreds of editions. Led the Catholic recovery in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland; died at Fribourg; Doctor 1925.

key: St Paul of the Cross, Confessor
patron_of: Passionists
prayer_title: St. Paul of the Cross Novena
blurb: Paolo Danei of Ovada in Liguria (1694–1775), who founded the Passionists in 1720 on Monte Argentario to preach the Passion in missions. Died at Rome; canonized 1867.

patron_of: inquisitors, midwives, against headaches
prayer_title: Novena to Saint Peter of Verona
blurb: Dominican preacher and inquisitor in Lombardy (c. 1205–1252), born of Cathar parents. Killed with an axe by a hired Cathar assassin on the road from Como to Milan on 6 April 1252; canonized eleven months later.

patron_of: Italy, Europe, nurses, the sick, firefighters, against fire, temptations, miscarriage
prayer_title: Litany in Honour of St. Catherine of Siena
blurb: Dominican tertiary (1347–1380) who persuaded Gregory XI to return the papacy from Avignon to Rome in 1377 and dictated the Dialogue. Received the stigmata in 1375; died at Rome aged 33.

key: St Joseph the Worker, Spouse of the BVM, Confessor
patron_of: workers, labourers, craftsmen, carpenters, fathers, families, the dying
blurb: Instituted by Pius XII on 1 May 1955 to give the workers' May Day a Christian meaning under the carpenter of Nazareth. It replaced the feast of the Patronage of St Joseph kept since 1847 after Easter.

patron_of: theologians
blurb: Bishop of Alexandria from 328 (c. 296–373), present at Nicaea as a deacon, exiled five times for defending the Son's full divinity against Arianism. Wrote On the Incarnation and the Life of Antony.

patron_of: mothers, wives, widows, difficult marriages, alcoholics, abuse victims, conversion of relatives
blurb: Mother of Augustine (331–387), from Tagaste in Numidia, married to the pagan Patricius. She followed her son to Milan and prayed for years until his baptism in 387; died at Ostia on the way home.

patron_of: Valletta, Malta
blurb: Dominican Antonio Ghislieri (1504–1572), pope from 1566, who issued the Roman Catechism, Breviary (1568), and Missal (1570) decreed by Trent. Formed the Holy League that won at Lepanto in 1571.

patron_of: Poland, Kraków, soldiers in battle
blurb: Bishop of Kraków from 1072 (1030–1079) who excommunicated King Bolesław II for his cruelty. The king killed him with his own hands while he said Mass at Skałka on 11 April 1079; canonized 1253.

key: St Gregory Nazianzen, Bishop, Confessor & Doctor
patron_of: poets
blurb: Cappadocian bishop (329–390), friend of Basil, called 'the Theologian' for the Five Theological Orations preached at Constantinople in 380. Briefly bishop of that city; resigned during the council of 381.

patron_of: St Philip: hatters, pastry-chefs, Luxembourg; St James: fullers, pharmacists, the dying
blurb: Philip of Bethsaida, who brought Nathanael to Jesus, and James son of Alphaeus, first bishop of Jerusalem, thrown from the Temple and clubbed in 62. The joint feast dates from the dedication of their basilica at Rome about 570.

key: Sts Nereus, Achilleus, Domitilla & Pancras, Martyrs
patron_of: St Pancras: children, oaths, against headaches, cramps, false witness
blurb: Nereus and Achilleus, soldiers who refused to serve, were beheaded in the late 1st century and buried in the catacomb of Domitilla. Domitilla, Domitian's niece, was exiled in 95; Pancras, aged 14, was beheaded at Rome in 304.

key: St Robert Bellarmine, Bishop, Confessor & Doctor
patron_of: catechists, catechumens, canon lawyers, canonists
blurb: Jesuit from Montepulciano (1542–1621) whose Controversies were the chief Catholic answer to Protestant theology. Cardinal from 1599, archbishop of Capua, and the one who delivered the 1616 warning to Galileo; Doctor 1931.

key: St John Baptist de la Salle, Confessor
patron_of: teachers, educators, school principals, students
prayer_title: Novena to Saint Jean-Baptiste de La Salle
blurb: Canon of Reims (1651–1719) who gave up his fortune to found the Brothers of the Christian Schools in 1680. Introduced free schools, classroom teaching in the vernacular, and the first training colleges for lay teachers.

patron_of: Gubbio, against demonic possession, migraine, neuralgia
blurb: Bishop of Gubbio in Umbria from 1129 (c. 1084–1160), remembered for walking out to face Frederick Barbarossa in 1155 and persuading him to spare the town. Gubbio still runs the Corsa dei Ceri on his eve.

patron_of: Camerino, against falls
blurb: Boy of fifteen martyred at Camerino in the Marches, traditionally under Decius about 250. His Acts are late and legendary; Clement X, a native of Camerino, raised the feast for the whole Church in 1670.

patron_of: bookbinders, hermits, L'Aquila, Molise
blurb: Hermit of the Maiella (c. 1215–1296) and founder of the Celestine monks, elected pope as Celestine V in July 1294 after a two-year vacancy. Resigned after five months; Boniface VIII confined him at Fumone, where he died.

patron_of: the Philippines
blurb: Roman virgin of the 2nd century, by tradition daughter of the senator Pudens who hosted Peter. Her title church on the Viminal is among the oldest in Rome; scholars suspect the name arose from 'ecclesia Pudentiana', the church of Pudens.

patron_of: advertising, public relations, communications, gambling addicts, chest ailments, hoarseness
blurb: Franciscan Observant preacher (1380–1444) who drew crowds across Italy and spread the IHS monogram of the Holy Name. Refused the sees of Siena, Ferrara, and Urbino; died at Aquila; canonized 1450.

patron_of: the sick and disabled, orphans, educators of girls, Ursulines
prayer_title: Litany in Honour of St. Angela Merici
blurb: Franciscan tertiary from Desenzano on Lake Garda (1474–1540) who founded the Company of St Ursula at Brescia in 1535, the first institute of women devoted to teaching girls, living at home without vows or enclosure.

patron_of: St Erasmus (Elmo): sailors, abdominal pain, colic, childbirth, Gaeta
blurb: Marcellinus, a priest, and Peter, an exorcist, were beheaded at Rome in 304 and buried on the Via Labicana; Damasus heard the story from their executioner. Both are named in the Roman Canon. Erasmus, bishop of Formiae, died about 303.

patron_of: Germany, brewers, file-cutters, tailors, Fulda
prayer_title: Litany in Honour of St. Boniface
blurb: Winfrid of Crediton (c. 675–754), sent by Gregory II to the Germans in 719; felled the Oak of Donar at Geismar, founded Fulda, and became archbishop of Mainz. Killed by pagans at Dokkum in Frisia on 5 June 754.

patron_of: Bohemia, Magdeburg, Antwerp, peace, safe delivery in childbirth
blurb: Canon of Xanten (c. 1080–1134), converted after a lightning strike, who founded the Premonstratensian canons at Prémontré in 1120 under the Rule of Augustine. Archbishop of Magdeburg from 1126.

Two elderly Roman brothers beheaded at Nomentum about 297 under Diocletian and buried on the Via Nomentana. In 648 Theodore I moved their bodies to Santo Stefano Rotondo, the first recorded translation of martyrs inside the walls.

key: St Margaret, Queen of Scotland, Widow
patron_of: Scotland, widows, large families, learning, queens, loss of children
blurb: Anglo-Saxon princess born in Hungary (c. 1045–1093), who married Malcolm III of Scotland about 1070. Brought Scottish usage into line with Rome, founded Dunfermline, and died four days after her husband fell at Alnwick.

patron_of: Cyprus, Antioch, Milan, peacemakers, against hailstorms
blurb: Levite of Cyprus named Joseph (Acts 4:36), who sold his field for the apostles, vouched for the converted Paul, and traveled with him on the first missionary journey. Tradition says he was stoned at Salamis in Cyprus about 61.

prayer_title: Litany of the Sacred Heart of Jesus
blurb: Kept on the Friday after the octave of Corpus Christi, honoring the love of Christ shown in his pierced heart. Grew from Margaret Mary Alacoque's visions at Paray-le-Monial in 1673–75; Pius IX extended it to the whole Church in 1856.

key: St Anthony of Padua, Confessor & Doctor
patron_of: lost articles, the poor, travellers, sailors, barren women, Portugal
prayer_title: Litany of Saint Anthony of Padua
blurb: Portuguese Franciscan (1195-1231), born in Lisbon as Fernando, who preached across Italy and southern France and died at Padua. Known for his Scripture-saturated sermons, he was named a Doctor of the Church in 1946.

patron_of: St Vitus: dancers, actors, epileptics, against oversleeping, Bohemia
blurb: Martyrs of Lucania in southern Italy, killed under Diocletian around 303; the acts make Vitus a Sicilian boy with his tutor and nurse. His relics reached Corvey in 836, spreading his cult through Germany.
Venetian nobleman (1625-1697), bishop of Bergamo and then Padua, and cardinal. He rebuilt the Padua seminary with a library and a press printing in Eastern languages; canonized in 1960 by John XXIII.

key: St Ephrem the Syrian, Deacon, Confessor & Doctor
patron_of: spiritual directors, spiritual leaders
blurb: Syriac deacon (c. 306-373) of Nisibis and later Edessa who wrote theology as hymns and verse homilies, earning the title Harp of the Holy Spirit. Benedict XV named him a Doctor in 1920.
Twin brothers of Rome, deacons by tradition, martyred under Diocletian about 286 after St Sebastian steadied their resolve. They were buried on the Via Ardeatina, where their tomb was found in 1902.

patron_of: the chronically ill, bodily ills
blurb: Florentine (1270-1341), niece of a founding Servite, who established the Servite Third Order sisters known as the Mantellate. Unable to swallow the Host when dying, she is said to have received it miraculously through her breast.

patron_of: Milan, haymakers, discovery of thieves
blurb: The first martyrs of Milan, of unknown date, whose bodies St Ambrose discovered in 386 and translated to his new basilica. The find, attended by reported healings, strengthened Ambrose against the Arian court.

patron_of: island of Ponza
blurb: Pope 536-537, son of Pope Hormisdas, who refused Empress Theodora's demand to reinstate the Monophysite patriarch Anthimus. Belisarius deposed and exiled him to the island of Palmaria, where he died of ill treatment.

patron_of: bell-ringers, bell-founders
blurb: Roman senator from Bordeaux (c. 354-431) who gave away a vast fortune, settled at the tomb of St Felix at Nola, and became its bishop. His letters and poems survive, including correspondence with Augustine and Jerome.

key: Nativity of St John the Baptist
patron_of: baptism, converts, tailors, monastic life, Jordan, Quebec, Puerto Rico
prayer_title: Litany to St. John the Baptist
blurb: Celebrates the birth of the Forerunner six months before Christmas, following Luke 1. Kept since the 4th century, it is one of only three birthdays on the Roman calendar, with those of Christ and Mary.
William of Vercelli (1085-1142), a hermit from Piedmont who settled on Monte Vergine near Avellino in 1119 and founded the Benedictine congregation that still keeps the Marian shrine there.

patron_of: against rain and lightning
blurb: Roman brothers, by tradition officers in the household of Constantine's daughter Constantia, executed secretly in their own house under Julian the Apostate in 362. The basilica on the Caelian stands over that house; both are named in the Roman Canon.

patron_of: St Peter: popes, fishermen, locksmiths; St Paul: missionaries, writers, theologians
prayer_title: Novena to Saints Peter and Paul
blurb: Joint feast of Rome's two founding apostles, both martyred under Nero in the 60s: Peter crucified on the Vatican hill, Paul beheaded on the Via Ostiensis. Rome kept June 29 by the year 258.

patron_of: missionaries, evangelists, writers, theologians, Malta, Rome
prayer_title: Novena to Saints Peter and Paul
blurb: The day after the joint feast, Rome honors Paul alone: apostle to the Gentiles, author of thirteen letters, beheaded at Aquae Salviae about 67 and buried where St Paul Outside the Walls now stands.

patron_of: popes, fishermen, locksmiths, net-makers, the universal Church
prayer_title: Litany of St. Peter, Prince of the Apostles
blurb: Commemoration of Peter within the Mass of St Paul on June 30, keeping the two apostles paired. Fisherman of Bethsaida, first bishop of Rome, crucified head downward under Nero about 64 and buried on the Vatican hill.

key: Most Precious Blood of Our Lord Jesus Christ
prayer_title: Litany of the Most Precious Blood of Jesus
blurb: Honors the Blood shed in the Passion as the price of redemption. Pius IX extended the feast to the whole Church in 1849 after his return from exile at Gaeta; Pius X fixed it on July 1 in 1914.

key: Visitation of the Blessed Virgin Mary
blurb: Commemorates Mary's journey to Elizabeth and the Magnificat (Luke 1:39-56). Kept by the Franciscans from 1263, it was extended to the whole Church by Urban VI in 1389 to pray for the end of the Western Schism.

patron_of: jailers, prison guards
prayer_title: Collect for the Feast of Saints Processus and Martinian
blurb: Roman martyrs buried on the Via Aurelia; later legend made them the Mamertine jailers converted by Peter and Paul. Their relics have rested in St Peter's since Paschal I moved them there in the 9th century.

Born in Smyrna about 130, a hearer of Polycarp, he became bishop of Lyon in 177 and wrote Against Heresies, the first systematic refutation of Gnosticism. He died about 202, traditionally as a martyr.

patron_of: Europe (co-patrons), Slavic peoples, ecumenism, unity of East and West
blurb: Brothers from Thessalonica sent to Moravia in 863, who devised the Glagolitic alphabet and translated the liturgy and Scriptures into Slavonic. Cyril died in Rome in 869; Methodius, archbishop of Pannonia, in 885.

key: St Elizabeth, Queen of Portugal, Widow
patron_of: peacemakers, brides, queens, Third Order Franciscans, against jealousy
blurb: Aragonese princess (1271-1336) married to King Denis of Portugal, remembered for riding between armies to reconcile her husband and their son. Widowed in 1325, she lived beside the Poor Clares at Coimbra.

key: Seven Holy Brothers, Martyrs, & Sts Rufina & Secunda, Virgins & Martyrs
prayer_title: Prayer on the Feast of the Seven Holy Brothers, and Sts. Ruffina and Secunda
blurb: The seven brothers, by tradition sons of St Felicitas, were martyred at Rome about 162 under Antoninus Pius and buried in four different cemeteries. Rufina and Secunda, Roman sisters, died under Valerian about 257 on the Via Cornelia.
Pope about 140-155, brother of Hermas, author of The Shepherd, according to the Muratorian fragment. His reign saw the condemnation of Marcion at Rome; his martyrdom is traditional and not recorded.

patron_of: bowel disorders
blurb: Franciscan from Bagnoregio (1221-1274), Minister General from 1257 and cardinal bishop of Albano, who died during the Second Council of Lyon. Author of the Itinerarium and the Life of Francis; Doctor of the Church since 1588, the Seraphic Doctor.

patron_of: the childless, the disabled, Benedictine oblates, kings, Finland, Basel
blurb: Duke of Bavaria (973-1024), king of Germany from 1002 and emperor from 1014, who founded the see of Bamberg in 1007 and promoted monastic reform. Married to St Cunegund; canonized in 1146.

prayer_title: Our Lady of Mount Carmel Novena
blurb: Feast of the Carmelite Order's Marian devotion, tied to the tradition of the brown scapular given to St Simon Stock in 1251. Kept by Carmelites from the 14th century, Benedict XIII extended it to the whole Church in 1726.

patron_of: beggars, pilgrims, nurses, Alexian Brothers
prayer_title: Prayer for the Feast of St. Alexius
blurb: A Roman of the 5th century, according to a legend from Edessa, who fled his wedding to live as a beggar in Syria, then returned and lived unrecognized for seventeen years under the stairs of his father's Aventine house.

patron_of: the sick, hospitals, nurses, physicians, against gambling
blurb: Soldier and gambler from the Abruzzi (1550-1614) who, after conversion, founded in Rome in 1582 the Ministers of the Sick, who nursed plague victims and the wounded on battlefields under a red cross on their habit.

key: Sts Symphorosa & her seven sons, Martyrs
prayer_title: Prayer for the Feast of St. Symphorosa and Her Seven Sons
blurb: Widow of the martyr Getulius, put to death at Tivoli under Hadrian around 120 for refusing to sacrifice at his new villa. She was drowned in the Anio and her seven sons killed the next day.

patron_of: orphans, abandoned children
blurb: Venetian soldier (1486-1537) who vowed himself to God while a prisoner in 1511 and devoted himself to orphans. He founded the Somaschi Fathers in 1532 and died of plague caught while nursing the sick.

patron_of: childbirth, pregnant women, nurses, kidney disease, the dying
prayer_title: Prayer for the Feast of St. Margaret of Antioch
blurb: Virgin martyr of Antioch in Pisidia, killed about 304 under Diocletian. Her legend, in which she bursts from a dragon that swallowed her, made her one of the Fourteen Holy Helpers; Joan of Arc named her among her voices.

key: St Lawrence of Brindisi, Confessor & Doctor
blurb: Capuchin (1559-1619), Minister General of his order, master of Hebrew and several languages, who in 1601 rode before the imperial army at Szekesfehervar holding a crucifix. John XXIII named him a Doctor in 1959.

Roman virgin of the 2nd century, daughter of the senator Pudens and sister of Pudentiana, said to have sheltered Christians and gathered martyrs' remains. Her titular church on the Esquiline dates from the 5th century.

patron_of: penitents, converts, perfumers, hairdressers, pharmacists, contemplative life
blurb: The woman of Magdala freed of seven demons who stood by the Cross and first saw the risen Christ. The Western tradition behind the title Penitent merged her with the sinful woman of Luke 7 and Mary of Bethany.

patron_of: Ravenna, against epilepsy and gout
blurb: First bishop of Ravenna, by tradition sent from Antioch by St Peter, martyred at the port of Classe in the 1st or 2nd century. The basilica of Sant'Apollinare in Classe was consecrated over his tomb in 549.

patron_of: against gallstones, colic and fevers; Paderborn
prayer_title: Prayer for the Feast of St. Liborius
blurb: Bishop of Le Mans in Gaul for nearly fifty years, dying about 397. The translation of his relics to Paderborn in 836 created a bond between the two cities that has lasted into modern times.

patron_of: millers, archers, mariners, Bolsena
prayer_title: Prayer for the Feast of St. Christina
blurb: Virgin martyr of Bolsena in Tuscany, killed about 304 under Diocletian. Her legend says she survived being thrown into Lake Bolsena with a millstone; her tomb lies in the catacomb beneath the basilica there.

patron_of: Spain, pilgrims, labourers, veterinarians, equestrians, arthritis sufferers
blurb: Son of Zebedee and brother of John, among the three closest to Jesus, beheaded by Herod Agrippa I in 44, the first apostle to die (Acts 12). His tomb at Compostela became the chief pilgrimage of medieval Europe.

patron_of: travellers, motorists, sailors, against storms, toothache, sudden death
blurb: Martyr in Lycia, Asia Minor, about 250 under Decius. The medieval legend of a giant who carried the Christ Child across a river grew from his name, Christ-bearer; he is one of the Fourteen Holy Helpers.

key: St Anne, Mother of the Blessed Virgin Mary
patron_of: mothers, grandmothers, housewives, miners, lace-makers, sailors, Brittany, Quebec
blurb: Mother of Mary, named with Joachim in the 2nd-century Protoevangelium of James. Her cult began in the East by the 6th century; Gregory XIII extended the feast to the whole Latin Church in 1584.

patron_of: physicians, midwives, livestock, against headaches; Fourteen Holy Helpers
prayer_title: Prayer for the Feast of St. Pantaleon
blurb: Physician to Emperor Galerius at Nicomedia, martyred under Diocletian about 305 after treating the poor without charge. One of the Fourteen Holy Helpers; a relic of his blood is kept at Ravello.

key: Sts Nazarius & Celsus, Martyrs, Victor I, Pope & Martyr, & Innocent I, Pope & Confessor
blurb: Nazarius and the boy Celsus were martyred at Milan, where Ambrose found their bodies in 395. Victor I, an African pope (189-199), pressed the Roman date of Easter; Innocent I (401-417) governed through the sack of Rome and condemned Pelagius.

patron_of: cooks, housekeepers, servants, innkeepers, waiters, dietitians
blurb: Sister of Mary and Lazarus at Bethany, who served Jesus at table and professed him the Christ before Lazarus was raised (John 11). Provencal legend brought her to Tarascon, where her tomb is venerated.

key: Sts Felix, Simplicius, Faustinus & Beatrice, Martyrs
blurb: Simplicius and Faustinus, brothers, were drowned in the Tiber about 303 under Diocletian; their sister Beatrice was strangled after burying them at Generosa on the Via Portuensis. Felix is the antipope Felix II, long mistaken for a martyr.

patron_of: coopers
prayer_title: Collect for the Feast of Saints Abdon and Sennen
blurb: Persian nobles, by their acts, brought to Rome as prisoners and martyred under Decius about 250 for refusing to sacrifice. They were buried in the cemetery of Pontian on the Via Portuensis, where a fresco of them survives.

patron_of: Jesuits, soldiers, retreats, spiritual exercises, Basque Country
blurb: Basque courtier and soldier (1491-1556), wounded at Pamplona in 1521, whose convalescent reading turned him to God. He wrote the Spiritual Exercises and founded the Society of Jesus, approved in 1540.

The seven brothers and their mother tortured to death under Antiochus IV Epiphanes about 167 BC for refusing to eat pork (2 Maccabees 7), the only Old Testament saints with a Roman feast. Relics rest at San Pietro in Vincoli.

patron_of: astronomers, scientists, the falsely accused, Dominican Republic
blurb: Castilian canon from Caleruega (1170-1221) who preached against the Albigensians in Languedoc and founded the Order of Preachers, approved in 1216. He died at Bologna, where his tomb remains.

key: Dedication of the Basilica of St Mary Major
prayer_title: Dedication of St. Mary Major Basilica Novena
blurb: Marks the dedication of the Esquiline basilica rebuilt by Sixtus III after the Council of Ephesus (431) proclaimed Mary Mother of God. The medieval legend of a miraculous August snowfall gave it the title Our Lady of the Snows.

key: Sts Sixtus II, Pope, Felicissimus & Agapitus, Martyrs
prayer_title: Prayer for the Feast of St. Sixtus and Companions
blurb: Pope Sixtus II was seized while preaching in the cemetery of Callixtus and beheaded on 6 August 258 under Valerian, with four deacons. The deacons Felicissimus and Agapitus died the same day and were buried in the cemetery of Praetextatus.

patron_of: the unemployed, job seekers, gamblers, bankers, workers, Argentina
blurb: Priest from Vicenza (1480-1547) who co-founded the Theatines in Rome in 1524 with Gian Pietro Carafa, the first order of clerks regular, to reform clerical life. He died at Naples.

patron_of: Arezzo, against epilepsy and lightning
blurb: Bishop of Arezzo in Tuscany in the 4th century, martyred by tradition under Julian the Apostate in 362. His acts tell of a shattered chalice made whole at Mass; his relics lie in the Arezzo cathedral.

patron_of: parish priests, confessors
blurb: Parish priest of Ars near Lyon (1786-1859), a struggling seminarian who became a confessor sought by pilgrims from across France, spending up to sixteen hours a day in the confessional. Canonized in 1925.

patron_of: St Cyriacus: eye disease, demonic possession, temptation at death; Fourteen Holy Helpers
prayer_title: Prayer for the Feast of St. Cyriacus, Largus and Smaragdus
blurb: Roman martyrs, Cyriacus a deacon, executed about 305 under Diocletian and Maximian. First buried on the Via Ostiensis, their remains were moved by Pope Marcellus to the Via Salaria; Cyriacus is a Fourteen Holy Helper.

patron_of: deacons, cooks, comedians, librarians, the poor, firefighters, Rome
blurb: Archdeacon of Rome, executed on 10 August 258 four days after Pope Sixtus II, by tradition roasted on a gridiron after presenting the poor as the Church's treasure. Constantine built the basilica over his tomb on the Via Tiburtina.
Tiburtius, a Roman martyr of about 286, was buried on the Via Labicana at the Two Laurels. Susanna, a Roman virgin, was martyred under Diocletian about 295; her titular church stands on the Quirinal.

patron_of: television, eye disease, embroiderers, goldsmiths, laundry workers, good weather
prayer_title: Prayer for the Feast of Saint Clare of Assisi
blurb: Noblewoman of Assisi (1194-1253) who followed Francis in 1212 and led the Poor Ladies at San Damiano for forty years. Her Rule, the first written by a woman, was approved two days before her death.

patron_of: St Hippolytus: horses, prison guards; St Cassian: schoolteachers, stenographers
blurb: Hippolytus, Roman priest and theologian, was exiled to the Sardinian mines in 235 and died there, reconciled with the Church. Cassian, a schoolmaster of Imola, was stabbed to death by his pupils with their styluses about 304.

Roman priest of the 4th century who founded the titular church of Sant'Eusebio on the Esquiline. His legend says the Arian emperor Constantius confined him in his house for seven months until he died.

key: Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary
blurb: Commemorates Mary's being taken body and soul into heaven at the end of her earthly life. Kept in the East by the 6th century and in Rome by the 7th, it was defined as dogma by Pius XII in 1950.

key: St Joachim, Father of the Blessed Virgin Mary
patron_of: fathers, grandfathers, grandparents, married couples
blurb: Father of Mary and husband of Anne, named in the 2nd-century Protoevangelium of James, where the childless couple receive the promise of a daughter. Pius X fixed his feast on 16 August in 1913.

patron_of: Poland, Lithuania, those in danger of drowning
blurb: Polish Dominican (c. 1185-1257) from Silesia who received the habit from Dominic in Rome in 1220 and preached across Poland, Prussia, and Kievan Rus. He died at Krakow, where his tomb is.

patron_of: against colic, Palestrina
blurb: A boy of fifteen martyred at Palestrina near Rome, by tradition under Aurelian about 274. His cult there is ancient; a basilica over his tomb existed by the 5th century.

Norman priest (1601-1680), first an Oratorian, who founded the Eudists in 1643 to run seminaries and the Sisters of Our Lady of Charity. He composed the first Masses and Offices of the Sacred Hearts of Jesus and Mary.

patron_of: Cistercians, beekeepers, candlemakers, Gibraltar, Burgundy
blurb: Burgundian (1090-1153) who entered Citeaux in 1112 and founded Clairvaux in 1115, from which Cistercian houses spread across Europe. He preached the Second Crusade in 1146 and was named a Doctor in 1830.

key: St Jane Frances Frémiot de Chantal, Widow
patron_of: forgotten people, widows, parents separated from children, in-law problems
blurb: Noblewoman of Dijon (1572-1641), widowed with four children in 1601, who with Francis de Sales founded the Visitation nuns at Annecy in 1610; eighty-seven houses existed at her death.

key: Immaculate Heart of the Blessed Virgin Mary
prayer_title: Novena to the Immaculate Heart of Mary
blurb: Honors Mary's interior life and love of God. Promoted by St John Eudes from 1648, the feast was extended to the whole Church by Pius XII in 1944, after his 1942 consecration of the world to the Immaculate Heart.

Timothy was martyred at Rome under Diocletian about 303 and buried near St Paul on the Via Ostiensis. Hippolytus was a bishop martyred at Porto in the 3rd century. Symphorian, a youth of Autun, was beheaded about 178.

patron_of: tanners, leatherworkers, bookbinders, butchers, plasterers, Armenia
blurb: Apostle listed in the Synoptic Gospels, commonly identified with Nathanael of Cana. Tradition sends him to India and Armenia, where he was flayed alive; relics claimed at Benevento and on the Tiber Island in Rome.

patron_of: France, French monarchy, Third Order Franciscans, barbers, builders, the sick
prayer_title: St. Louis King of France Novena
blurb: Louis IX of France (1214-1270), king from age twelve, who built the Sainte-Chapelle for the Crown of Thorns and led two crusades. He died of disease at Tunis and was canonized in 1297.

prayer_title: Collect for Saint Zephyrinus, Pope and Martyr
blurb: Pope 199-217 during the Modalist and Adoptionist disputes, criticized by Hippolytus for leniency. He died under Caracalla and was buried in the cemetery on the Via Appia that bears his deacon Callixtus's name.

patron_of: Catholic schools, students, schoolchildren, Piarists
blurb: Aragonese priest (1557-1648) who opened in Rome in 1597 the first free public school in Europe and founded the Piarists to staff such schools. He was deposed by intrigue within his order before his death.

patron_of: theologians, printers, brewers, sore eyes, Augustinians
blurb: Born at Thagaste in North Africa in 354, converted at Milan in 386, bishop of Hippo from 395 until his death in 430 during the Vandal siege. His Confessions and City of God shaped all later Western theology.
Roman martyr of the early 2nd or 3rd century, buried in the cemetery of Basilla on the Via Salaria Vetus. His feast appears in the Depositio Martyrum of 354; legend made him a prefect of Rome.

key: Beheading of St John the Baptist
patron_of: baptism, converts, tailors, monastic life, Jordan, Quebec, Puerto Rico
prayer_title: Litany to St. John the Baptist
blurb: Commemorates John's execution by Herod Antipas at Salome's request (Mark 6). The date comes from the dedication of a church at Sebaste in Samaria, his traditional tomb; Rome kept it by the 5th century.

patron_of: housewives
blurb: Roman matron martyred under Hadrian about 126, according to her acts, after conversion by her slave Serapia. The 5th-century basilica of Santa Sabina on the Aventine stands on the site identified as her house.

patron_of: expectant mothers, midwives, childbirth, newborns, the falsely accused, secrecy of confession
prayer_title: Collect for the Feast of Saint Raymond Nonnatus
blurb: Catalan Mercedarian (c. 1204-1240) who ransomed Christian captives in Algiers and gave himself as hostage when money ran out; his captors reportedly padlocked his lips. Named cardinal, he died at Cardona en route to Rome.

patron_of: beggars, the disabled, lepers, blacksmiths, breastfeeding, Edinburgh; Fourteen Holy Helpers
prayer_title: Collect for the Feast of Saint Giles
blurb: Hermit of the 7th or 8th century near Nimes in Provence, said to have been wounded by a king's arrow aimed at the hind that fed him. The abbey of Saint-Gilles grew over his tomb; a Fourteen Holy Helper.

Twelve African martyrs who died under Valerian about 258, whose relics Duke Arechis II gathered at Benevento in 760. The legend that they were sons of St Boniface and St Thecla of Hadrumetum grew from that translation.

patron_of: Hungary, kings, bricklayers, stonemasons
blurb: First king of Hungary (c. 975-1038), crowned about 1000 with a crown sent from Rome, who organized his realm into dioceses and counties. His right hand is venerated at Budapest; canonized in 1083.

patron_of: first communicants, pilgrims, catechists, Patriarchate of Venice
blurb: Giuseppe Sarto (1835-1914), patriarch of Venice, pope from 1903, who admitted children to early Communion, restored Gregorian chant, began codifying canon law, and condemned Modernism in 1907. Canonized in 1954.

patron_of: Venice
blurb: Venetian (1381-1456), a founder of the canons of San Giorgio in Alga, who in 1451 became the first Patriarch of Venice. He wrote ascetical treatises and lived in deliberate poverty in office.

key: Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary
prayer_title: Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary Novena
blurb: Celebrates the birth of Mary nine months after the Immaculate Conception. The date derives from the dedication of the church of St Anne in Jerusalem; Pope Sergius I added it to the Roman calendar in the late 7th century.

patron_of: soldiers, arms dealers, butchers, prison guards, against plague and epilepsy
blurb: Officer at Nicomedia converted by the courage of Christians he was persecuting, martyred about 306 under Galerius; his wife Natalia tended him in prison. His relics went to Constantinople and later Rome.
Roman martyr buried on the Via Labicana at the Two Laurels, listed in the Depositio Martyrum of 354. Later legend conflated him with Gorgonius the chamberlain martyred at Nicomedia in 303.

patron_of: holy souls in purgatory, mariners, infants, animals, the dying
blurb: Augustinian friar (c. 1245-1305) who preached and heard confessions at Tolentino in the Marche for thirty years. Known for austerity and reported miracles, he was the first Augustinian canonized, in 1446.

prayer_title: Collect for the Feast of Saints Protus and Hyacinth
blurb: Roman martyrs of the 3rd century, by tradition brothers, buried in the cemetery of Basilla on the Via Salaria Vetus. Hyacinth's sealed tomb, found intact by de Rossi in 1845, is the only Roman martyr's grave recovered undisturbed.

prayer_title: Litany of the Blessed Virgin Mary (of Loreto)
blurb: Honors the name of Mary as the Holy Name of Jesus is honored. Granted to Cuenca in Spain in 1513, it was extended to the whole Church by Innocent XI in 1683 after the relief of Vienna from the Turks.

key: Seven Sorrows of the Blessed Virgin Mary
prayer_title: Litany of Our Lady of Seven Sorrows
blurb: Commemorates the seven griefs of Mary, from Simeon's prophecy to the burial of Christ. A Servite devotion from the 13th century; Pius VII extended the September feast to the whole Church in 1814.
A Roman priest and martyr of uncertain date, buried on the Via Nomentana. The Martyrology says he was beaten to death with leaded whips for refusing to sacrifice; little else is known.

key: Sts Cornelius, Pope, & Cyprian, Bishop, Martyrs
patron_of: St Cornelius: cattle, against earache, fever, epilepsy; St Cyprian: North Africa, Algeria
blurb: Cornelius was pope 251 to 253 and died in exile at Civitavecchia; Cyprian, bishop of Carthage, was beheaded in 258 under Valerian. Allies by letter, both resisted the rigorists over readmitting lapsed Christians.

patron_of: St Euphemia: Chalcedon, Rovinj
blurb: Euphemia was a virgin martyred at Chalcedon about 303; her basilica there housed the council of 451. Lucy and Geminian are recorded as martyrs at Rome of uncertain date, joined to her on this day.

key: Impression of the Stigmata of St Francis, Confessor
patron_of: St Francis: animals, ecology, merchants, Italy, Franciscans
prayer_title: Litany to St. Francis of Assisi
blurb: Commemorates Francis of Assisi receiving the wounds of Christ on Mount La Verna in September 1224, two years before his death. Kept by the Franciscans, the feast was extended to the universal calendar by Paul V in 1615.

patron_of: aviators, astronauts, students, exam-takers, the mentally handicapped
prayer_title: Novena to St. Joseph of Cupertino
blurb: Italian Conventual Franciscan priest from Apulia (1603-1663), slow-witted as a youth, famed for repeated levitations during Mass and prayer, which led his superiors to keep him in seclusion for decades. Canonized 1767.

patron_of: Naples, blood banks, against volcanic eruptions
blurb: Bishop of Benevento, beheaded at Pozzuoli near Naples about 305 under Diocletian with six companions. A vial of his blood kept in Naples cathedral is reported to liquefy on his feast.

patron_of: accountants, bankers, tax collectors, bookkeepers, customs officers
blurb: Tax collector of Capernaum called by Christ from his customs booth; traditionally author of the first Gospel, written for Jewish Christians. Later tradition sends him to Ethiopia or Persia; relics claimed at Salerno since the 10th century.

key: St Thomas of Villanova, Bishop & Confessor
patron_of: Valencia, Villanova University, the poor
blurb: Spanish Augustinian friar (1486-1555), archbishop of Valencia from 1544; known for giving away nearly his whole income to the poor and reforming a long-neglected diocese. Canonized 1658.

patron_of: St Maurice: soldiers, infantry, swordsmiths, dyers, weavers, Switzerland, Savoy
prayer_title: Collect for Saints Maurice and Companions, Martyrs
blurb: Officers and soldiers of the Theban Legion, Christian Egyptians said to have been massacred at Agaunum (now Saint-Maurice, Switzerland) about 286 under Maximian for refusing to join pagan rites or persecute Christians.
Second pope, successor of Peter, about 67 to 76; named by Irenaeus and perhaps in 2 Timothy 4:21. His martyrdom is traditional rather than attested; buried near Peter on the Vatican hill.

prayer_title: Novena to Our Lady of Ransom
blurb: Commemorates the founding of the Mercedarian Order by St Peter Nolasco at Barcelona in 1218 to ransom Christian captives from the Moors, attributed to a vision of Mary. Extended to the universal calendar in 1696.

key: Sts Isaac Jogues, John de Brébeuf & Companions, Martyrs (North American Martyrs)
patron_of: North America, Canada, missionaries
blurb: Eight French Jesuits and lay helpers killed by Mohawk and Iroquois warriors between 1642 and 1649 in what are now upstate New York and Ontario, Jogues in 1646 and Brébeuf in 1649. Canonized 1930.

patron_of: Bohemia, Czech Republic, Prague, brewers
blurb: Duke of Bohemia (about 907-935), raised Christian by his grandmother St Ludmila; murdered at the church door of Stará Boleslav by followers of his brother Boleslav. Honored since as Bohemia's chief saint.

key: Dedication of St Michael the Archangel
patron_of: St Michael: soldiers, police, paramedics, grocers, mariners, the dying, the Church
prayer_title: Litany of St. Michael the Archangel
blurb: Commemorates the dedication of a basilica to St Michael on the Via Salaria north of Rome, probably in the 5th century. The oldest Michael feast of the Roman rite; it also recalls his apparition on Monte Gargano.

patron_of: librarians, scholars, translators, students, archaeologists
blurb: Born in Dalmatia about 347, secretary to Pope Damasus, settled in Bethlehem from 386 until his death in 420; translated the Bible into Latin from Hebrew and Greek, the Vulgate, and wrote commentaries and sharp polemics.

patron_of: France, Reims, against epidemics, fevers, religious indifference
prayer_title: Prayer for the Feast of Saint Remigius
blurb: Bishop of Reims for more than 70 years (about 437-533); baptized Clovis, king of the Franks, with some 3,000 of his warriors about 496, beginning the conversion of the Franks to Catholic Christianity.

patron_of: protection, travellers, children, police
prayer_title: Litany of the Holy Guardian Angel
blurb: Honors the angels assigned to guard each person, a belief drawn from Matthew 18:10 and Psalm 90. Kept in Spain by the 16th century; Clement X fixed it on October 2 for the whole Church in 1670.

key: St Teresa of the Child Jesus, Virgin
patron_of: missions, missionaries, France, florists, aviators, the sick, AIDS sufferers
prayer_title: Litany to St. Therese of the Child Jesus
blurb: Carmelite nun of Lisieux, Normandy (1873-1897), who entered at 15 and died of tuberculosis at 24; her autobiography Story of a Soul set out her little way of confidence in small things. Canonized 1925.

patron_of: St Placid: novices, against chills and drowning
prayer_title: Collect for the Feast of Saint Placid and His Companions
blurb: Placid was a boy disciple of St Benedict at Subiaco in the 6th century. A medieval forgery made him a martyr at Messina, Sicily, with 30 companions killed by raiders about 541; the cult outlived the discredited story.

patron_of: Carthusians, Calabria, Germany, against demonic possession
blurb: Born in Cologne about 1030, master of the cathedral school at Reims; in 1084 withdrew with six companions to the Chartreuse valley near Grenoble, founding the Carthusians. Died in 1101 at his second hermitage in Calabria.

prayer_title: Novena to Our Lady of the Rosary
blurb: Instituted by Pius V as Our Lady of Victory after the Christian fleet defeated the Turks at Lepanto on October 7, 1571, a victory credited to the rosary. Clement XI extended it to the whole Church in 1716.
Pope for eight months in 336, successor of Sylvester I; founded the church of San Marco in Rome and a cemetery basilica on the Via Ardeatina, where he was buried.

patron_of: Sweden, Europe, widows, scholars
prayer_title: Novena to St. Bridget of Sweden
blurb: Swedish noblewoman (about 1303-1373) and mother of eight who after her husband's death founded the Brigittine order at Vadstena; lived in Rome from 1349 urging the popes to return from Avignon. Her Revelations were widely read.

key: Sts Sergius, Bacchus, Marcellus & Apuleius, Martyrs
patron_of: Sts Sergius & Bacchus: soldiers, Syria, Arab Christians
prayer_title: Novena to Saint Sergius and Saint Bacchus
blurb: Sergius and Bacchus were Roman officers martyred in Syria about 303; Sergius's tomb at Resafa became a major pilgrimage shrine. Marcellus and Apuleius are Roman martyrs of uncertain date buried near the city.

patron_of: pharmacists, Lucca, Clerks Regular of the Mother of God
prayer_title: Prayer for the Feast of Saint John Leonardi
blurb: Pharmacist's apprentice turned priest of Lucca (1541-1609); founded the Clerks Regular of the Mother of God in 1574 and helped start the college that became Propaganda Fide. Died in Rome nursing plague victims.

key: Sts Denis, Bishop, Rusticus & Eleutherius, Martyrs
patron_of: St Denis: France, Paris, against headaches, frenzy, strife, the possessed
blurb: Denis, first bishop of Paris, sent from Rome about 250, was beheaded with the priest Rusticus and deacon Eleutherius on Montmartre. Their tomb became the abbey of Saint-Denis, burial place of the French kings.

patron_of: Portugal, against earthquakes
prayer_title: Prayer for the Feast of Saint Francis Borgia
blurb: Spanish duke of Gandía (1510-1572) and great-grandson of Pope Alexander VI; widowed, he joined the Jesuits in 1546 and became their third superior general in 1565, expanding the missions and founding the Roman College.

key: Maternity of the Blessed Virgin Mary
prayer_title: Litany of Mary, Mother of God
blurb: Celebrates Mary as Mother of God, the title defined against Nestorius at the Council of Ephesus in 431. Pius XI instituted the feast in 1931 for the council's 1,500th anniversary.

patron_of: England, English kings, difficult marriages, separated spouses
blurb: King of England from 1042 to 1066, the last of the old West Saxon line; built Westminster Abbey, where he is buried. Canonized in 1161 for his piety and reported miracles.

patron_of: cemetery workers
prayer_title: Prayer for the Feast of Saint Callistus I, Pope, Martyr
blurb: Pope 217 to 222, a former slave who had managed the Christian cemetery on the Via Appia that bears his name; opposed by Hippolytus for leniency toward penitents. Died in Trastevere, traditionally in a riot.

key: St Teresa of Jesus (of Ávila), Virgin
patron_of: Spain, headache and illness sufferers, lacemakers, religious, the loss of parents
prayer_title: Litany to St. Teresa of Avila
blurb: Carmelite nun of Ávila (1515-1582) who from 1562 founded the reformed Discalced Carmelites, 17 convents in all; her Life, Way of Perfection and Interior Castle are classics of mystical theology. First woman named Doctor (1970).

patron_of: Silesia, Poland, Berlin, brides, widows, duchesses, difficult marriages, death of children
blurb: Bavarian-born duchess of Silesia (about 1174-1243), wife of Henry the Bearded; founded the Cistercian convent at Trebnitz and retired there after his death in 1238. Canonized 1267.

patron_of: devotees of the Sacred Heart, polio sufferers, loss of parents
prayer_title: Litany of Saint Margaret Mary Alacoque
blurb: Visitation nun of Paray-le-Monial, Burgundy (1647-1690), who between 1673 and 1675 reported visions of Christ asking for devotion to his Sacred Heart, including a feast on the Friday after Corpus Christi. Canonized 1920.

patron_of: physicians, surgeons, artists, painters, notaries, butchers, bachelors
blurb: Greek physician of Antioch, companion of Paul, author of the third Gospel and Acts and the only Gentile New Testament writer. Tradition says he died in Boeotia aged 84; relics claimed at Padua.

patron_of: Brazil, Extremadura, night watchmen, eucharistic adoration
prayer_title: Novena to Saint Peter of Alcantara
blurb: Spanish Franciscan (1499-1562) who founded the austere Discalced reform in Extremadura; known for extreme penances, sleeping an hour and a half a night for decades, and as counselor to Teresa of Ávila. Canonized 1669.

patron_of: Poland, Lithuania, professors, students, pilgrims
blurb: Priest and professor of theology at the University of Kraków (1390-1473), born at Kęty in Silesia; known for learning, several pilgrimages to Rome on foot, and giving his goods to poor students. Canonized 1767.

patron_of: hermits, Cyprus
blurb: Born near Gaza about 291, disciple of Anthony in Egypt; introduced monasticism to Palestine about 306, then fled his fame to Sicily, Dalmatia and Cyprus, where he died in 371. His Life was written by Jerome.

patron_of: St Ursula: students, schoolgirls, teachers, Cologne, Ursulines, a holy death
prayer_title: Novena to Saint Ursula and Companions
blurb: A British princess and her virgin companions, said to have been killed by Huns at Cologne while returning from Rome, perhaps in the 4th or 5th century. A 4th-century inscription attests virgin martyrs at Cologne; the figure 11,000 is medieval.

key: St Anthony Mary Claret, Bishop & Confessor
patron_of: weavers, textile merchants, savings banks, Catholic press, Claretians, Cuba
prayer_title: Novena to St. Anthony Mary Claret
blurb: Catalan weaver's son and preacher (1807-1870); founded the Claretian missionaries in 1849, was archbishop of Santiago de Cuba 1850 to 1857 and confessor to Queen Isabella II, and died in exile in France.

patron_of: travellers, the sick, physicians, nurses, happy meetings, the blind, young people, lovers
blurb: One of the three archangels named in Scripture; in the Book of Tobit he guides young Tobias, binds the demon Asmodeus and heals Tobit's blindness. Benedict XV placed him on the universal calendar in 1921.
Pope about 97 to 105, successor of Clement; the Liber Pontificalis credits him with dividing Rome into titular parishes. Called a martyr by tradition though no account survives; buried near Peter.

patron_of: St Jude: desperate and hopeless cases, hospitals; St Simon: curriers, sawyers, tanners
blurb: Simon the Zealot and Jude Thaddeus, apostles about whom the Gospels say little; Jude is credited with the short epistle bearing his name. Tradition says they preached in Persia and were martyred together there; relics at St Peter's.

Honors all the saints, known and unknown. It grew from the dedication of the Pantheon to Mary and the martyrs on May 13, 609; Gregory IV extended the November 1 observance to the whole Church about 835.

patron_of: bishops, catechists, seminarians, spiritual directors, against ulcers and intestinal disorders
blurb: Cardinal-nephew of Pius IV at 22 (1538-1584), archbishop of Milan from 1564; helped bring the Council of Trent to a close and enforced its reforms through seminaries, synods and visitations. Nursed Milan through the plague of 1576.
Martyrs at Bologna under Diocletian about 304; Vitalis, the slave of Agricola, died first under torture and Agricola was crucified. Ambrose discovered their bodies in 393 and spread the cult.

key: Dedication of the Archbasilica of the Most Holy Saviour (Lateran)
blurb: Commemorates the dedication by Pope Sylvester, about 324, of the basilica Constantine built on the Lateran estate, the cathedral of Rome and mother and head of all churches. First dedicated to the Savior, later also to the two Johns.

patron_of: soldiers, recruits, Venice, Brindisi, against storms
blurb: Soldier called Tyro, the recruit, burned at Amasea in Pontus about 306 after setting fire to a temple of Cybele. One of the most honored Eastern martyrs; the church of San Teodoro stands below the Palatine in Rome.

patron_of: Naples, Sicily, against sudden death, apoplexy and stroke
blurb: Neapolitan lawyer (1521-1608) who became a Theatine priest after telling a lie in court; spent decades reforming convents and preaching in Naples and Lombardy. Collapsed from a stroke while beginning Mass. Canonized 1712.

patron_of: St Tryphon: gardeners, vine-growers, against pests and rodents
blurb: Tryphon, a gooseherd of Phrygia, was martyred at Nicaea about 250 with Respicius; Nympha was a virgin of Palermo of uncertain date. Their relics were brought together at Rome, hence the common feast.

patron_of: soldiers, France, beggars, tailors, innkeepers, vintners, horses, geese
prayer_title: Novena to Saint Martin of Tours
blurb: Soldier from Pannonia (about 316-397) who divided his cloak with a beggar at Amiens; founded Ligugé, the first monastery in Gaul, and was bishop of Tours from 371. Among the first non-martyrs given a public cult.

patron_of: merchants, travellers, caravans, falsely accused
blurb: Egyptian soldier martyred under Diocletian about 300; his shrine at Abu Mina west of Alexandria was a major pilgrimage center of the 5th and 6th centuries, whose oil flasks have been found across the Mediterranean.

prayer_title: Prayer for the Feast of Saint Martin, Pope
blurb: Pope 649 to 655, who condemned Monothelitism at the Lateran Synod of 649 against the imperial edict; arrested by Constans II, tried at Constantinople and exiled to the Crimea, where he died. The last pope honored as a martyr.

patron_of: immigrants, emigrants, hospital administrators, orphans
blurb: Founded the Missionary Sisters of the Sacred Heart in Lombardy in 1880 (1850-1917); sent by Leo XIII to Italian immigrants in New York in 1889, she opened 67 schools, hospitals and orphanages. First United States citizen canonized (1946).

patron_of: Franciscan lay brothers, San Diego, against sore throat
prayer_title: Prayer for the Feast of Saint Didacus
blurb: Spanish Franciscan lay brother from Andalusia (about 1400-1463); served in the Canary Islands and nursed the sick at Rome's Aracoeli during the 1450 jubilee; died at Alcalá. Canonized 1588 after a cure attributed to him of Philip II's son.

patron_of: Ukraine, Christian unity, Eastern Catholics
blurb: Basilian monk and Byzantine-rite archbishop of Polotsk (about 1580-1623) who worked for union of the Ruthenian Church with Rome; killed by a mob at Vitebsk. The first Eastern saint formally canonized by Rome (1867).

patron_of: the West Indies, souls in Purgatory, travellers, against mice and rats
prayer_title: Litany in Honour of Saint Gertrude the Great
blurb: Nun of Helfta in Saxony (1256-about 1302) from the age of five; her Herald of Divine Love records visions centered on the heart of Christ, an early form of Sacred Heart devotion. Known as Gertrude the Great.

patron_of: against earthquakes, floods, desperate and forgotten causes
prayer_title: Prayer to Saint Gregory the Wonder Worker
blurb: Pupil of Origen at Caesarea, bishop of Neocaesarea in Pontus from about 240 to 270; said to have found 17 Christians there and left 17 pagans. Called the Wonderworker for miracles including moving a mountain.

key: Dedication of the Basilicas of Sts Peter & Paul
prayer_title: Novena to Saints Peter and Paul
blurb: Commemorates the dedication of the Constantinian basilicas over the tombs of Peter on the Vatican hill and Paul on the Ostian Way, and the consecration of the new St Peter's by Urban VIII on November 18, 1626.

patron_of: bakers, beggars, brides, widows, hospitals, nurses, charities, Third Order Franciscans
prayer_title: Litany in Honour of Saint Elizabeth of Hungary
blurb: Daughter of King Andrew II (1207-1231), married at 14 to Landgrave Louis of Thuringia; widowed at 20, she became a Franciscan tertiary and spent her last years nursing the poor in a hospital she built at Marburg. Canonized 1235.

Pope 230 to 235, deported with Hippolytus to the mines of Sardinia by Maximinus Thrax; resigned the papacy, the first pope known to do so, and died there. His body was brought back to the cemetery of Callistus.

patron_of: Trinitarians, captives
prayer_title: Prayer for the Feast of Saint Felix of Valois
blurb: Hermit of the Valois region (1127-1212) who with St John of Matha founded the Trinitarian Order at Cerfroid in 1198 to ransom Christian captives. His life is known mostly from later Trinitarian tradition.

key: Presentation of the Blessed Virgin Mary
prayer_title: Litany of the Life of Mary
blurb: Commemorates Mary's being brought as a child to the Temple in Jerusalem, a story from the 2nd-century Protoevangelium of James. Kept in the East from the 6th century; extended to the whole Church by Sixtus V in 1585.

patron_of: mariners, sailors, stonecutters, marble workers, blacksmiths
prayer_title: Novena to Saint Clement of Rome
blurb: Third successor of Peter, pope about 88 to 97; his letter to the Corinthians is the earliest Christian writing outside the New Testament. Later legend has him exiled to the Crimea and drowned with an anchor.

patron_of: mothers, parents who have lost children, against sterility
blurb: Roman widow martyred about 165 under Marcus Aurelius after watching her seven sons die; buried in the cemetery of Maximus on the Via Salaria. The sons are honored July 10; the story's historicity is debated.

key: St John of the Cross, Confessor & Doctor
patron_of: contemplatives, mystics, Spanish poets
prayer_title: Litany in Honour of Saint John of the Cross
blurb: Castilian Carmelite (1542-1591) who joined Teresa's reform in 1568; imprisoned nine months at Toledo by the unreformed friars, where he began the Spiritual Canticle. His Ascent, Dark Night and Living Flame earned him the title Doctor in 1926.
Martyr beheaded at Aquileia about 304 under Diocletian; his cult was carried to Rome, where the title church of San Crisogono in Trastevere bears his name and he is named in the Roman Canon.

patron_of: philosophers, students, scholars, lawyers, librarians, unmarried girls, wheelwrights, millers, nurses
prayer_title: Novena to Saint Catherine of Alexandria
blurb: Virgin of Alexandria said to have confounded 50 philosophers before the emperor Maxentius, been bound to a spiked wheel that broke, and been beheaded about 305. No early evidence survives; her shrine at Mount Sinai dates from the 9th century.

patron_of: Sylvestrine Benedictines
blurb: Sylvester Gozzolini (1177-1267), a canon of Osimo who became a hermit after seeing the decayed corpse of a once-handsome relative; founded the Sylvestrine Benedictines at Montefano near Fabriano in 1231.

key: St Peter of Alexandria, Bishop & Martyr
blurb: Bishop of Alexandria from 300 and head of its catechetical school; set rules for readmitting the lapsed and opposed Arius's early teaching. Beheaded in 311 under Maximinus Daia, the last martyr of the persecution there.

patron_of: Scotland, Russia, Greece, fishermen, fishmongers, singers, rope-makers, against sore throats
blurb: Fisherman of Bethsaida, brother of Simon Peter and the first disciple called in John's Gospel; preached in Greece and was crucified at Patras, traditionally on an X-shaped cross. Relics were taken to Constantinople in 357.

patron_of: against hangovers, headaches, epilepsy, mental illness, single laywomen
blurb: Roman virgin said to have been scourged to death about 363 under Julian the Apostate; the church of Santa Bibiana on the Esquiline was built over her tomb in the 5th century and rebuilt by Bernini in 1624.

patron_of: foreign missions, missionaries, navigators, India, Japan, Australia, Borneo, Goa
prayer_title: Litany in Honour of Saint Francis Xavier
blurb: Navarrese nobleman (1506-1552) and one of the first Jesuits; from 1542 a missionary in India, the Moluccas and Japan, baptizing tens of thousands. Died on Shangchuan Island awaiting entry into China. Canonized 1622.

key: St Peter Chrysologus, Bishop, Confessor & Doctor
patron_of: Imola, Ravenna, against fever and rabies
blurb: Bishop of Ravenna, then the imperial capital, from about 433 to 450; surnamed golden-worded for his short, plain sermons, some 180 of which survive. Declared Doctor in 1729.

patron_of: artillerymen, miners, firefighters, architects, against lightning, sudden death
blurb: Virgin said to have been shut in a tower by her pagan father, who beheaded her himself and was struck dead by lightning, at Nicomedia in the 3rd century. No early evidence; the cult spread from the 7th century.

Cappadocian monk (439-532) who founded the Great Laura, Mar Saba, in the Judean desert in 483, still inhabited; led the Palestinian monks against Monophysitism and twice went to Constantinople to plead with the emperors.

patron_of: Milan, beekeepers, bees, candlemakers, learning, students
blurb: Roman governor acclaimed bishop of Milan in 374 while still a catechumen (about 340-397); faced down the Arian court and the emperor Theodosius, wrote hymns and doctrinal works, and baptized Augustine in 387.

key: Immaculate Conception of the Blessed Virgin Mary (Patroness of the USA)
patron_of: United States of America, Portugal, Spain, Brazil, Philippines, Korea
blurb: Celebrates Mary's preservation from original sin from the first moment of her conception, defined as dogma by Pius IX in 1854. Clement XI made the feast universal in 1708; the US bishops placed the country under this title in 1846.

Pope 311 to 314, an African; saw Constantine's victory and the end of persecution, received the Lateran palace, and presided over the Roman synod of 313 on the Donatists. Called a martyr for his sufferings under Maximian.

patron_of: archaeologists
prayer_title: Novena to Saint Pope Damasus I
blurb: Pope from 366 to 384 after a violently contested election; commissioned Jerome's revision of the Latin Bible, adorned the martyrs' tombs in the catacombs with verse inscriptions, and pressed the claims of the Roman see.

patron_of: the Americas, Mexico, the unborn
prayer_title: A Prayer to Our Lady of Guadalupe
blurb: Commemorates the apparitions of Mary to the Indian Juan Diego on Tepeyac hill near Mexico City in December 1531 and the image left on his tilma, kept in the basilica there. Feast approved for New Spain in 1754.

patron_of: Vercelli
blurb: Bishop of Vercelli from 345, the first in the West to live in community with his clergy; exiled to the East by Constantius II in 355 for refusing to condemn Athanasius. Died 371; honored as a martyr for his sufferings.

patron_of: architects, builders, construction workers, surveyors, India, Sri Lanka, against doubt
blurb: The apostle called Didymus who doubted the Resurrection until he touched the wounds; tradition sends him to India, where the St Thomas Christians trace their origin to him and he was speared at Mylapore near Madras about 72.

patron_of: deacons, stonemasons, bricklayers, horses, against headaches
blurb: One of the seven deacons of Jerusalem; stoned outside the city about 34 to 36 after his speech before the Sanhedrin (Acts 6-7), with Saul of Tarsus looking on. His relics were reported found at Caphargamala in 415.

patron_of: theologians, writers, authors, editors, publishers, booksellers, friendship, against poison and burns
prayer_title: Novena to Saint John the Apostle and Evangelist
blurb: Son of Zebedee, the beloved disciple, by tradition author of the fourth Gospel, three epistles and Revelation; cared for Mary after the Crucifixion, was exiled to Patmos, and died at Ephesus about 100, the only apostle not martyred.

patron_of: babies, children, choirboys, foundlings
blurb: The male children of Bethlehem aged two and under killed by Herod the Great in his attempt to destroy the infant Christ (Matthew 2:16). Honored since the 5th century as martyrs in deed though not in will.

key: St Thomas of Canterbury, Bishop & Martyr
patron_of: secular clergy, Exeter College Oxford, Portsmouth
prayer_title: Prayer for St. Thomas a Becket
blurb: Chancellor of Henry II (1118-1170), then archbishop from 1162; defended clerical jurisdiction against the king, spent six years in French exile, and was killed by four knights in his cathedral on December 29. Canonized 1173.

Pope 314 to 335 during Constantine's reign; the Lateran, St Peter's and other basilicas were built in his pontificate, and he sent legates to the Council of Nicaea in 325. Buried in the cemetery of Priscilla on the Via Salaria.
